name: Carrot Alternaria leaf spot
symptoms: Dark brown to black spots on leaves Angular lesions with yellow margins Spots appear first on older leaves Spots merge and form large dead areas Leaves become black, dry and wither Severe infection causes leaf blight and plant weakening Seedlings may die from damping-off
description: Alternaria leaf spot is a fungal disease that mainly affects carrot leaves. It starts on older leaves and produces dark spots with yellow margins. In severe infections the leaves turn black, dry and die, causing major yield loss.
management: Use certified disease-free seeds Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 25–30 minutes) Avoid dense planting to reduce humidity Remove infected crop debris after harvest Rotate crops for at least 3 years Grow tolerant carrot varieties
